## Failure modes

- A new Make target without shard wiring can miss CI shard coverage.
- A new harness without `python/checks.py` mapping can miss focused relevant checks.
- A new shell harness absent from the design SKILL wrapper inventory can fail agent-lint orphan checks.
- A representative-only direct-target test can miss one required design module mapping.
- A README anchor without a `docs/skills.md` section creates a broken catalog link.
- A mismatched brainstorm sink can log failures that collect mode cannot ingest.
- A collect-mode harness that omits `agent collect-results` can fail before the behavior under test.
- A collect-mode harness that omits `run-log append-failure` can skip the External Reviewer Issues behavior under test.
- Running the OOS checkpoint after stats or manifest stamping can preserve false-complete state.
- Reimplementing checkpoint logic in `oos_filer.py` can drift from the existing CLI.
- Sentinel-only recovery without accepted-OOS evidence can fail the real checkpoint.
- Checkpoint failure after filing can re-file the same accepted batch unless persisted evidence is reused first.
- Treating `oos-issues.ndjson` alone as Step 9a.1 completion can hide checkpoint failure.
- Broad upgrade cleanup globs can delete runtime files.
- Duplicated autofix ok rows can pollute execution issues.
- Emitting the autofix ok audit before rc override can attach false success evidence.
- Omitting `--site` from the autofix ok audit can make `run-log append-failure` fail.
- Using the overwritten validator log instead of `ORIGINAL_VALIDATE_LOG_FILE` can attach stale or empty evidence.
